These high pore volume mesoporous silica, together with SBA-15, will be used for fabricating HNC and PEF loaded with HNC. 3.2. HNC and PEF Fabrication and Characterization 3.2.1. HNC Fabrication and Structure and Composition Characterization A PA coating was generated on the outer surface of mesoporous silica (SBA-15 and high pore volume mesoporous silica) loaded with amines by interfacial polymerization to seal amines. Once the silica pores were entirely filled, an interfacial reaction was performed to generate a dense coating at the pore mouth. The underlying reaction is the Schotten-Baumann reaction, involving a reactant containing an acid chloride group and another reactant with an amine group, where the two functional groups react to synthesize an amide structure. This reaction can become a 19 2 0 0 n m 1 0 0 n m 2 0 0 n m polymerization reaction using molecules such as TMC and amines, like DETA, which have multiple available functional groups, resulting in thermally stable and dense coatings. With this understanding, a coating was generated by reacting amine-loaded SBA-15 or high pore volume mesoporous silica with a solution of TMC in hexane for a desired amount of time. During the process of coating development, influence of different reaction parameters on the coating quality was investigated. The purpose was to generate a coating which can seal amines in silica pores and thus maintain consistent CO uptake during long-term thermal treatment. Different parameters 2 studied were concentration of TMC in hexane or tulene, amount of TMC that the amine-loaded SBA-15 is exposed to, the reaction time, the stirring rate, and water/amine loading.
